patch.value:
## Repro (real data)

1. pm create + pm update --release 2026.6.1 + pm close (closed_at = today)
2. Multi-window: pm-changelog --all-release-tags -> item under '## 2026.6.1' (correct, honors release)
3. Single-window: pm-changelog --release-version 2026.7.24 --since <today> -> item under '## 2026.7.24' (wrong, ignores release)

## Fix direction

Honor the release field in the single-window path behind an opt-in flag so default output stays byte-identical for the 18 fleet consumers whose CI runs changelog:check.
Single-window generation ignores an item release field, retro-dating already-shipped work

Duplicate check: searched all statuses for release field attribution shipped-in retro-date closed_at window pin single-window; existing pmc-vl87/pmc-ew5n cover item REFERENCE rendering only, and no item covers release attribution in the single-window path. pm-changelog places an item from itemTimestamp() = closed_at ?? updated_at ?? created_at. The multi-window path (--all-release-tags / assignItemsToReleaseWindows) additionally PINS an item into the window whose tag matches the item release field regardless of timestamps, but the single-window path used by every fleet repo changelog / changelog:check / release:notes script ignores the release field entirely. Consequence: a tracker whose fix shipped in release X but whose item is closed later lands in the CURRENT release window, so the changelog claims months-old work as new, and the two generation paths disagree about the same item.

Single-window generation honors an item release field (top-level or metadata) under an opt-in flag; An item pinned to a release other than the window version is excluded from that window; An item pinned to the window version is included regardless of its timestamp; Default output stays byte-identical when the flag is absent; --explain reports items excluded by release attribution

Multi-agent workflows routinely ship a PR in one release and close the tracker in a later one; without release attribution the changelog is wrong and agents are forced to leave trackers open forever (3 such items across the fleet today).

value.text: Root cause of the fleet-wide shipped-but-unclosed tracker backlog (pmc-sall, pm-csv-69ln, pm-slack-gx2h): closing them today would inject their entries into the current release window.

value.text: Reproduced with real data in a throwaway pm workspace: item with release=2026.6.1 closed 2026-07-24 renders under 2026.6.1 via --all-release-tags but under 2026.7.24 via --release-version 2026.7.24 --since 2026-07-24T00:00:00Z.

value.author: claude-opus-5
value.text: Any time-window report keyed on closed_at silently misattributes work when the tracker is closed after the release that shipped it; an explicit release field is the only durable attribution signal.
